name: High-grade astrocytoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Histological evidence of astrocytic tumor with increased cellularity, mitotic activity, and nuclear atypia
Presence of necrosis and/or microvascular proliferation on histology
Molecular features such as IDH mutation status and 1p/19q co-deletion to classify tumor subtype

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of high-grade astrocytic tumor with necrosis or microvascular proliferation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular profiling is increasingly important for classification and prognosis

searchTerms: gradual worsening of localized neurological problems
progressive weakness or numbness in one area

common.symptomName: Headache with increased intracranial pressure features
searchTerms: headache with signs of high brain pressure
headache with nausea and vision changes
weakness on one side of body

occasional.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting related to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting from brain pressure
vomiting related to increased head pressure
feeling sick due to raised intracranial pressure
loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: CSF analysis typically non-specific but may show elevated protein
imaging: MRI showing contrast-enhancing mass with necrosis and surrounding edema
T1 hypointense and T2 hyperintense lesion with irregular borders
genetic: TERT promoter mutations and MGMT promoter methylation status
other: Histopathological confirmation via biopsy or resection specimen

distinguishingFeatures: Lower mitotic activity and absence of necrosis
Different histological appearance with round nuclei

redFlags: New-onset seizures in adult without prior history
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Omuro A, DeAngelis LM. Glioblastoma and other malignant gliomas: a clinical review. JAMA. 2013.
Weller M, et al. EANO guidelines on the diagnosis and treatment of diffuse gliomas of adulthood. Nat Rev Clin Oncol. 2021.
